BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every material point. Several items are framed as "negotiated positions," but no fallback has been authorised. The 20% cap is the only Seller position that sits near a playbook fallback, and that fallback needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft, which hasn't been given. The Seller's cover note calls the package "fair and balanced." It is not. It shifts most of the risk to the Buyer, and several of its statements are contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.

## Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start; 20% only with Frost written authority | Opens at our fallback; no authority given |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, deductible (excess only) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | 5x higher and deductible rather than tipping |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 needs Frost approval) | Shorter, no approval |
| Limitation spillover (12.3/13) | Any general limitation applies to all Claims | No hidden general-regime override | Would override fundamental/title |
| Fundamental/Title (12.x) | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge | Fundamentally different regime |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to max extent enforceable | No fraud carve-out at all |
| Disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Sch 7) | Whole data room, public registers, Accounts | Specific fair disclosure only | Deemed general disclosure |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Excludes anything known or discoverable from data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusion; named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry | Blanket exclusion, can reach title and fraud |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent AND evidence of conditions pre-Completion | Consent-on-delivery; endeavours insufficient |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release provided after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases | Post-completion release without undertaking or approval |
| Employee bonuses (DD-005) | Excluded from funds flow; "a matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or seller-funded, including triggered on-costs | Silently excluded |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure | Narrow and no independent verification |
| Export/privacy incident (4.6/Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates | Materiality conclusion unsupported |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt or price deduction | Pre-judged characterisation |
| Tax/IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Open; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution | Assumes resolution we haven't agreed |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences 100% title | Independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence required | Relies on seller-supplied internal source |

## Material issues and reasoning

**1. Liability architecture (cap, basket, de minimis, time).** The combined effect is a materially weaker general regime. A AUD 25,000 de minimis combined with a deductible AUD 250,000 basket means the first AUD 250,000 of losses is unrecoverable, and small claims below AUD 25,000 are excluded entirely. The 18-month period also cuts the window for latent defects. Our playbook sets a 25% / AUD 6m cap as the opening position, so the Seller's 20% opener is already at our fallback before any negotiation.

**2. Fundamental and title claims folded into the general regime.** This is the most serious structural issue. Capacity and title warranties are the core protection of a share purchase. Applying general caps, time limits and the "any limitation applies to all Claims" clause would expose the Buyer to a cap of AUD 4.8m on title, a 18-month window, and the basket and de minimis. The playbook requires a separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years. Our playbook says there is no hidden general-regime override.

**3. No fraud carve-out.** The Seller's limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" with no exception. Our playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct to be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, and no one may waive this. This is a non-negotiable item.

**4. Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** Disclosing the entire data room, public registers and the Accounts as general disclosure, combined with clause 8.3 excluding anything "discoverable," would effectively convert the Buyer's diligence into a waiver. Combined, these would allow the Seller to argue that any issue in the data room is disclosed against all warranties, and that the Buyer cannot claim for anything it could have found. Our playbook rejects both and requires specific disclosure with named knowledge persons.

**5. Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).** The Seller's own disclosure (item 2) states there is no final written consent and no evidence that conditions are satisfied. The cover letter says the consent is "addressed" and treats it as satisfied on delivery. Our playbook requires effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is not enough for a material customer consent.

**6. Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m outstanding).** The Seller's disclosure (item 3) says the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. The cover letter proposes a release "following Completion." Our playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval. Paying off the Seller's debt from Completion funds should be the default.

**7. Employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs).** The funds flow excludes the bonuses while the cover letter says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics." These two statements can't both be right. The bonuses are conditional, and the disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply. The playbook requires a specific line item or seller funding, including triggered on-costs.

**8. Ironquay IP.** The indemnity is restricted to the SOW3 payment. The AUD 180,000 open amount is not verified, and the disclosure says no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment exists. The Seller's "adequate" characterisation is unsupported. Our playbook requires a broader indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. We should not accept or reject the AUD 180,000 figure without independent bank or ledger evidence.

**9. Export/privacy incident (DD-006).** The Seller describes this as "not expected to be material," but its own disclosure says the investigation is preliminary, the scope is unknown and notification requirements are not determined. The material involves up to ~1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps. We should not assume a breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure in either direction. Our playbook requires log preservation, investigation and regular updates. We should also consider whether a specific indemnity is needed. This is a judgement call for the deal team, since the playbook doesn't specify one.

**10. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs. The disclosure says whether each is terminable, unavoidable or accrued is not stated, and the renewals should be read together for timing and scope. Our playbook requires assessment without automatic Debt classification or price deduction. We should ask for each contract's terms, notice periods and whether they are a related series.

**11. Tax and IP.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." The playbook keeps them open with no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution. This is a substantive issue: under the Seller's approach, tax and IP would be capped and time-limited like general warranties. These must stay in separate categories.

**12. Title evidence.** DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal share register. The playbook says this is not independent proof. We need independent evidence: an ASIC company extract, a PPSR search, confirmation that no encumbrances exist over the shares, and evidence of the Seller's capacity and authority.

**13. Other items for follow-up.** The office lease (DD-007) notes a notification obligation, and the disclosure says it is not described as a landlord consent requirement. The Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009) is similar. Neither is covered by the playbook explicitly. We should confirm in writing whether any consent is required for the share sale, and not accept the Seller's assumption.

**14. Inconsistencies in the Seller's cover note.** The cover note says the Bluefen consent is "addressed" and Riverlark will be released after Completion. The Seller's own disclosure says neither has been satisfied. The cover note also calls its positions "KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS," but no such negotiation has taken place. These should be corrected in writing so they are not treated as agreed.

## Recommendations

**Reject outright:**
- The 25% / AUD 6m starting cap is ours; reject the 20% cap unless Frost gives written authority identifying the draft.
- The AUD 25,000 de minimis, AUD 250,000 deductible basket and 18-month period.
- Applying general limitations to fundamental and title claims, and the "any limitation applies to all Claims" clause.
- The absence of a fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out.
- Whole data room, public registers and Accounts as general disclosure.
- Clause 8.3's blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion.
- Consent-on-delivery for Bluefen and reasonable endeavours as the standard.
- Post-completion Riverlark release without an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
- Tax and IP being settled under the general regime.
- DD-012 as sufficient title evidence.

**Counter-propose:**
- Our 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket and 24-month period.
- A separate title/capacity regime at 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- A fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all limitations, to the maximum extent enforceable, with no waiver.
- Specific fair disclosure only, with named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry for any knowledge qualifier.
- Bluefen: effective written consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion.
- Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases.
- Bonuses: a specific funds-flow line item for AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs, or seller funding.
- Ironquay: broadened indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure, with payment evidence for the AUD 180,000.
- DD-006: log preservation, investigation, regular updates; consider a specific indemnity.
- Sandbar: contract review and assessment, with no automatic price deduction.
- Tax and IP: keep open and separate from the general regime.
- Title: independent ASIC, PPSR and encumbrance searches plus Seller capacity evidence.

**Seek clarification:**
- Whether any landlord or Mossvale consent is required for the share sale.
- Written correction of the cover note's statements on Bluefen, Riverlark and "negotiated positions."

**Process:**
- Do not treat any Seller position as agreed.
- Any concession beyond our starting positions requires Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft.
- Have NSW-qualified counsel review the final mark-up, particularly the title regime, fraud carve-out and disclosure wording.
